title: South Africa's Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
angle: The Norwegian Nobel Committee gave the 2026 Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, 85, the South African judge, 'for her efforts to promote peace and international law'. Lead with the award and the committee's own words, then what she actually did, as the reports give it: the Rwanda tribunal bench, the International Criminal Court, UN human rights chief, and the UN commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory, whose genocide finding is why the feed tags the word; state that finding exactly as the reports do and attribute it. The mechanism: a prize for international law in a year when the courts that apply it are under sanction and attack, so say which governments welcomed it and which objected, each attributed. Hindustan Times adds her grandparents were Indian indentured labourers in Natal; one clause. Al-Monitor carries the Reuters text. Dateline Oslo.

title: South Africa pulls asylum directive after violent protests
angle: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs withdrew a directive telling its offices to accept asylum applications and judge them on their merits, after anti-immigrant protests turned violent in Durban and Soweto. Lead with the reversal and who it lands on: asylum seekers who can again be turned away on procedural grounds before anyone hears their case. The mechanism: say what the directive said and which court ruling it answered (the Constitutional Court is tagged), who organised the protests and what was attacked, how many were hurt or arrested, and what misinformation about the directive circulated, as the reports give it. The structural point: a government dropped a measure its own courts required because of street violence. Daily Maverick's report from Friday morning has the director-general's withdrawal and the local detail: https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-09-home-affairs-scraps-asylum-seeker-directive-after-violence-in-durban-and-soweto/ . Dateline Johannesburg, or Pretoria if the reports file the decision from there.

title: Trump envoys pitching 'new ideas' to settle Ukraine conflict - media -- RT World News
angle: The new development since the Kramatorsk bus-stop bombing (covered 10-08, one clause; the toll is now at least 35 in the Guardian): Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly accused the United States of being unwilling to help Ukraine, while Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukrainian negotiators and, Axios reports via Meduza, carry 'new ideas' and plan to go to Moscow this month. Lead with that collision: the president of the country being bombed says Washington will not help on the day Washington's envoys say they have a plan. The mechanism: say what Zelenskyy asked for (wider Starlink access to target ballistic-missile launchers) and why that is in one company's and one government's gift, what is known of the envoys' ideas and what is not, and what Kyiv and Moscow each said. Write from the Guardian, the Reuters text on Yahoo, Ukrainska Pravda and Meduza; RT is Russian state media and is used only where the independent reports agree. The feed title is RT's; write your own. Dateline Kyiv.

title: 3 killed in Saudi Arabia after Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
angle: The new development since the 10-08 piece on the second day of strikes and the oil price (one clause): Yemen's Houthis now say a ballistic missile hit Riyadh's airport and badly damaged a plane, and airlines have begun suspending flights to the Saudi capital. Lead with the suspensions, which are verifiable, then the claim, marked as a claim: Saudi Arabia has not commented on it and has confirmed only the three killed in the airport strikes earlier this week, so do not present the three dead as a result of this latest strike. The mechanism: say which airlines stopped flying and for how long, what a closed or half-closed Riyadh means for a Gulf already cut off by sea, what the Houthis say they are answering (the coalition's air campaign in Yemen, including the Sanaa school-bus strike covered 10-08, one clause), and what Saudi air defences did. Count the dead on both sides with the authority that gave each figure. Dawn is the regional outlet in the cluster; no Saudi or Gulf outlet carried it. Dateline Riyadh.

title: Zack Polanski faces greatest crisis of his leadership so far
angle: Sagal Abdi-Wali, who arrived in Britain as a child refugee from Somalia in the 1990s and grew up in Camden, won the Holborn and St Pancras by-election in north London. Lead with the result, not the BBC's leadership-crisis frame: who won, for which party, by what margin and on what turnout, and why the seat was vacant, each as the reports give it; state nothing about party or margin that the pages do not. The mechanism: the Greens under Zack Polanski had been expected to take the seat, so say what went wrong for them, what the result says about Labour and Keir Starmer, and why Andy Burnham is in the story. Who it matters to: a Somali-born Muslim woman now holds one of the most watched seats in British politics; Al Jazeera's pre-vote report says what the campaign was fought on, Gaza included if it says so. The New York Times may be paywalled. Dateline London.

title: Russia ready to help Iran resolve conflict with US-Israel: Putin
angle: Vladimir Putin told Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian on Thursday that Moscow is ready to help resolve Iran's conflict with the United States and Israel, and Pezeshkian confirmed that talks with Washington will continue. Lead with Pezeshkian's confirmation, which is the news: after a week of reports that the Pentagon was drafting strike options before the US midterms (covered 10-08, one clause), Tehran says the channel is open. The mechanism: say where they met (the Commonwealth of Independent States summit; Turkmenistan is tagged), what Putin actually offered and whether anyone accepted it, what format the US-Iran talks take and who mediates them, and what Russia gains from the role. An offer is an offer: no agreement was announced. Single source, an Indian outlet carrying agency copy; Mehr, Iranian state media, reports Pezeshkian at the same summit (https://en.mehrnews.com/news/248436/Pezeshkian-stresses-expansion-of-Armenia-ties-in-all-fields) and may be used for the venue only. Dateline the summit city as the report gives it.

title: India Scraps Key Tax Relief for Gold Imports, Raising Costs
angle: India let a tax exemption on banks' imports of gold, silver and platinum lapse, and banks have been paying a 3% integrated goods and services tax on bullion since April, the revenue secretary confirmed. Lead with the odd part: the world's second-largest gold buyer raised the cost of importing it six months ago and it is only now public. The mechanism: say what the relief was, how the 3% tax works (paid up front at import, recoverable later, so it ties up banks' capital), who it lands on (the banks that bring in bullion, then jewellers and households for whom gold is savings), and why the government did it: to curb imports and protect the rupee and the trade balance, only as the reports say. Name the series plainly: the price of gold. Give the gold price and India's import volumes only as Reuters gives them. Bloomberg may not fetch; write from Reuters. Dateline Mumbai.

title: Brazil's Bolsonaro Promises a Sharp Pivot on Climate and the Amazon
angle: New since the 10-08 piece on Flávio Bolsonaro's pension pledge (one clause): the front-runner in Brazil's 25 October runoff against President Lula is promising to reverse course on climate and the Amazon, and Reuters reports that the tight race has put Brazil's climate-finance push in doubt. Lead with the money and the forest: which funds and commitments depend on who wins (the forest-finance facility Brazil has been raising money for, the Amazon Fund, donor pledges, each only as the reports name them), and what Bolsonaro says he would do about enforcement and deforestation targets. The mechanism: donors and investors commit against a government's policy, so a credible chance of reversal freezes money before a vote is cast; give the deforestation figures under each previous government only as the reports do. Al Jazeera adds that a Supreme Court judge issued an arrest warrant for his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro: one sentence, attributed. A campaign promise is a promise. Bloomberg may not fetch; write from Reuters and Al Jazeera. The Hindu page is a video of student protests. Dateline Brasília, or the city Reuters files from.

title: Factcheck: UK Conservatives double the ‘cost of net-zero’ after spreadsheet blunder
angle: A booklet published by Britain's opposition Conservative Party puts a 'cost of net-zero' figure at the centre of its case against climate policy, and Carbon Brief's analysis finds the number appears to have been doubled by a spreadsheet error. Lead with the two numbers: what the booklet claims and what the same sources give when the sum is done correctly. The mechanism for a numerate reader: say exactly what the error was (what was counted twice, or which column was added to which), where the underlying figures come from, and what a gross cost leaves out, such as the fuel not bought; then what the party said when asked. The structural point: a headline number that will be repeated through an election cycle rests on arithmetic nobody checked before publication. Attribute the finding to Carbon Brief and use its 'appears to' where it does. Single specialist source. Dateline London.

title: We're still figuring out the side effects of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs
angle: Research presented this week at an ageing meeting in Boston found that overweight and diabetic people taking GLP-1 drugs score younger on at least some measures of biological age, MIT Technology Review reports, alongside a still-growing list of side effects. Lead with the finding and its size, stated exactly as the page does, and say at once what it is: a conference presentation, not a published trial. The mechanism: say what 'biological age' measures here (which clock or biomarker), whether the effect is separable from weight loss itself, who ran the study and in how many people, and then what the page reports on side effects and what remains unknown. The page is a weekly column: take the findings and their sources from it and leave out the first-person framing. Who it matters to: these drugs are taken by tens of millions and priced out of reach in most of the world. Give the article a dateline and location: Boston, where the research was presented. US dateline (1 of 3).

title: MARA transfers $81.1 million in bitcoin (BTC) to Galaxy Digital as strategy pivots to AI
angle: MARA Holdings, one of the largest bitcoin miners, moved about 996 BTC ($81m) to an address identified as Galaxy Digital's, after cutting its holdings by 18,245 BTC between February and August to pay down debt and build AI computing infrastructure. Lead with the larger number, not the day's transfer: a company whose business was accumulating bitcoin has been selling it to become a data-centre operator. The mechanism for a technical reader: a miner's real assets are power contracts, grid connections and cooled buildings, which AI computing now pays more for than mining does; say what MARA is building and for whom, what the shift does to the network's hash rate and to who is left mining, and that the destination address is an attribution by a chain-analytics firm, not a company statement. Name the series plainly: the price of bitcoin, in one clause, with no price commentary. Single specialist source. Give the article a dateline and location: the city of MARA's headquarters as CoinDesk gives it. US dateline (2 of 3).

title: Co-creator of Empire Market dark web marketplace given 40-year sentence
angle: Raheim Hamilton, 30, co-creator of the Empire Market dark-web marketplace, was sentenced to 40 years in a US prison after pleading guilty to a drug conspiracy charge and agreeing to forfeit more than $100m in bitcoin and several properties in Virginia. Lead with the sentence and the forfeiture. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what Empire Market was and how large (listings, users, sales volume, as The Record gives them), how it operated (Tor, cryptocurrency escrow) and how it ended, how investigators identified its operators and traced the bitcoin, and what happened to the co-defendant. The point worth a sentence: 40 years for running the platform rather than selling on it sets the going rate for marketplace operators. Give nothing the page does not; the feed entry was a two-line teaser. Single specialist source. Dateline the city of the sentencing court as The Record gives it. US dateline (3 of 3). The feed's pubDate is in the future (10 October, 00:55 GMT): check it against the page.
